rounds.response:
Given our strong documentary and witness record, we should refuse to let Opposing Counsel cabin discovery or control the narrative with a premature partial‑summary‑judgment timetable; instead use the 26(f) process to secure broad, targeted production (schedules, change orders, all project communications, PM/financial system exports and relevant ESI), preserve depositions to test post‑hoc explanations, and be prepared to move for narrow, early dispositive relief ourselves after targeted discovery if appropriate.  
Proposed discovery plan to present: 5–6 months fact discovery; rolling productions starting within 30 days of the 26(f) report for core categories; an ESI protocol and initial custodial collections (propose 8–12 custodians per side with reservation to add); up to eight fact depositions per side subject to leave to seek additional depositions if justified; expert discovery to proceed after fact discovery (no stay).  
Frame the joint 26(f) report to reject their unilateral early‑briefing request, stress proportionality but not undue restriction, ask the court to defer any dispositive‑motion schedule until substantial completion of fact discovery, and note either side may seek narrow early dispositive relief after targeted productions.  
Draft email for you to send as‑is: "Counsel — We received your letter and do not agree that discovery should be so narrowly cabined or that expert discovery should be stayed. Given our substantial documentary and witness evidence of contractual performance and your client's post‑hoc defenses, we will not accept your proposed limits; instead we propose a 5–6 month fact discovery period with rolling productions beginning within 30 days covering project schedules, change orders, all communications, financial/PM system exports, an ESI protocol and initial custodians (8–12 per side) with leave to add custodians, up to eight fact depositions per side (subject to leave to add), and expert discovery to follow fact discovery (no stay); if you intend to file an early partial summary judgment motion before targeted productions are complete, we will oppose it and reserve the right to pursue our own narrow early dispositive motion following targeted discovery; please confirm your availability to meet and confer so we can submit a joint 26(f) report consistent with this approach."  
We can shorten or tailor the proposed custodians and categories in the meet‑and‑confer, but we will not agree to an artificially constrained schedule that prejudices our ability to test the other side's manufactured defenses.

rounds.response:
Strategic assessment: accept their concession on duration — agree to a five‑month fact discovery period with rolling productions beginning 30 days after initial disclosures and pragmatically accept up to six fact depositions per side — but draw a hard line refusing any blanket stay of expert discovery and refusing to let the parties’ entire schedule be hard‑wired around their anticipated partial‑SJ motion; expert discovery should follow fact discovery, and either party must retain the right to bring narrow, early dispositive motions after targeted productions, with us prepared to take the dispute to the Court if they insist on a one‑sided structure.  

Proposed discovery‑plan language to circulate (copy‑ready): "Five‑month fact discovery; rolling productions to commence within 30 days of initial disclosures covering core categories (project schedules, all change orders, all project‑related communications, project/financial/PM system exports, invoices/payments, and relevant ESI); ESI protocol to include initial custodial collections (10 custodians per side) with reservation to add custodians and targeted search terms; up to six fact depositions per side, subject to leave to seek additional depositions for good cause; expert discovery to follow the close of fact discovery (no blanket stay); neither party waives the right to move for narrow, targeted dispositive relief after substantial completion of core productions."  

Talking points for the 26(f): your proposal is one‑sided because it freezes expert discovery and seeks to lock the schedule around your anticipated motion; your partial‑SJ plan is premature until core ESI collections and key witness depositions test whether your defenses are post‑hoc; we will insist in the joint report on no blanket expert stay and on both sides' equal right to pursue targeted early dispositive relief after document production, and if you persist we will present a competing schedule to the Court and move for judicial resolution.
